overall_summary: Analysis of 47 unique videos shows that first-person sensory survival hooks ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme cosmic anomaly deep-dives consistently drive 5x to 10x higher engagement and view velocity (800-1,050 views, 20-38 likes) compared to generic trivia. In contrast, recycled psychology facts and duplicate re-uploads (e.g., octopus hearts, earworms, fake memories) suffer extreme audience fatigue with views collapsing below 50.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Hypothetical Survival / Extreme Sensory Plunge
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) outperformed standard trivia titles by 400%+.
winning_patterns.action: Use the high-stakes 'What If You Fell Into...' or cinematic survival scenario structure with visceral visceral sensory descriptions (temperature, pressure, sight).

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,028 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) generated channel-leading retention and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Frame exoplanetary and cosmic phenomena around physics contradictions (e.g., burning cold, crushing light, backward time).

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated uploads of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' flatlined at 5, 10, and 53 views; earworm facts hovered at 17 to 71 views.
weak_patterns.action: Halt generic neuro-trivia rehashes and abstract brain facts lacking narrative tension or visual stakes.

weak_patterns.pattern: Duplicate Video Uploads with Identical Hooks
weak_patterns.evidence: Triple uploads of 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' (34-220 views) and 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (118-363 views) yielded diminishing returns.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict deduplication; rotate fresh subject entities instead of reposting variations of previously covered facts.

next_video.concept: What If You Stepped Onto KELT-9b: The Vaporized Metal World
next_video.opening_direction: Start directly inside the descent: 'If you stepped out onto KELT-9b, your spacecraft would melt into glowing plasma before you even touched the atmosphere.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the planet is so blisteringly hot that iron and titanium exist as glowing atmospheric clouds, tearing its own molecules apart into atomic shred.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-conversion 'What If You Fell/Stepped Into' survival hook on a completely untouched extreme astronomical body (KELT-9b, hotter than most stars), maximizing click-through and curiosity retention.
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not feature Gliese 436b (burning ice), 55 Cancri e (diamond planet), HD 189733b (glass rain), TrES-2b (darkest planet), WASP-76b (iron rain), or Venus.
Must not repeat octopus hearts, shark age comparisons, or brain memory trivia.

experiment: Test whether framing the opening hook around instant personal survival sensory consequences ('Your spacesuit would vaporize in 0.3 seconds') delivers higher retention at the 5-second mark than passive exoplanet trivia statements.
